answer: Like a lotus that only blooms after roots take hold in the tundra of cold open data, an agent earns trust by locking a small refundable bond per identity and completing verifiable tasks over time. Each finished job adds to a public reputation trail, so one real agent builds an echo of honest work a fresh fake cannot copy. Spawning a thousand sybils means locking a thousand bonds and doing a thousand jobs first, which costs more than the attack gains, while any proven fraud slashes the bond.
